clue.text: Excitement evident screening sparkling stuff in "From Here To Eternity"

indicators.note: screening means hiding something behind or within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a visible state of excitement is a fever, as in a fever of anticipation
or is the heraldic word for gold, a sparkling metal

explanation.surface: Someone notices the thrill shown by a champagne-like drink featured in the famous war film.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title in quotation marks is the definition; 'Excitement evident' is a visible fever of excitement. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A span from now until eternity is endless time, which is what the adverb means.

clue.text: Fake that's Dutch, unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a fraud is a fake or impostor

explanation.surface: A forgery revealed to be Dutch, though not completed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney slang, 'Dutch' (from duchess) means wife, so it is the definition, not a nationality. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is German for wife, and old Dutch is Cockney slang for one's wife.

clue.text: Powerful card cut at the top and bottom

indicators.note: cut at the top means the first letter is removed, the top in a down entry

parts.note: a trump outranks other cards

explanation.surface: A strong card is trimmed at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top and bottom' reads as one phrase, but 'bottom' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rump is a word for the buttocks or backside.

clue.text: Something to do, note, unfortunately prohibited

parts.note: a verb is a doing word

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A task and a memo are, sadly, banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges NOTE into OTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Verboten is German for forbidden, used in English for something not allowed.

clue.text: On top, go over again

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: Revisiting what was said at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or go over the main points once more.

clue.text: Occupier of tank is mortally wounded by the Spanish

parts.note: someone mortally wounded dies
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A tank crewman is fatally hit by Spanish forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The tank is a fuel tank, not an armoured vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel fuel is what fills the fuel tank of many vehicles, so it occupies it.

clue.text: South American shrub piercing ripe cactus

indicators.note: piercing suggests going through, here running across the words

explanation.surface: A thorny plant pokes into a ripe cactus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac is a South American plant whose root yields an emetic.

clue.text: Soap found under bum, which is sweet

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means coming after the other piece

parts.note: to bum is to sponge or cadge
soap comes in a cake

explanation.surface: A bar of soap discovered beneath someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' is a verb, to cadge, not the body part. 'which is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge cake is a light dessert, and sweet is a British word for a pudding.

clue.text: Greek character threading needles made clothes in Austria

indicators.note: threading means passing through, so one piece runs inside the other
made means formed or fashioned, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek tailor threads needles to make Austrian clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges the letters of needles, and 'threading' slips the Greek letter through the middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are leather shorts traditionally worn in Austria and Bavaria.

clue.text: Escalation of military power 'urts people

parts.note: a Cockney dropping the H says 'urts for hurts, and the H-less harms gives this
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker complains that a military build-up hurts ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'urts signals a dropped H, so harms loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: An arms race is a competitive build-up of weapons between rival nations.

clue.text: Back in a tick

definitions.meaning: to back a proposal is to support it formally
a tick is a very short moment of time

explanation.definitionFit: Second is both a verb for supporting a motion and a noun for a brief instant.

clue.text: Those working with tool

definitions.meaning: people who ply a trade are those who work at it
a gripping hand tool with two hinged jaws

explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a gripping tool and also, literally, people who ply.

clue.text: Double jeopardy securing work, then left in fix

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside, so one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: jeopardy is danger
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for fix

parts.note: to fix something in place is to peg it

explanation.surface: A legal phrase about being tried twice, with work and a left-hander caught in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double jeopardy' looks like a single legal term, but 'Double' alone is the definition. 'then' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A doppelganger is a person's exact double or lookalike.

clue.text: Signal to in both directions, beginning to point quickly?

parts.note: the word to written forwards and then backwards gives this run of four letters

indicators.note: to here means attached into, so the letter joins the other piece

parts.note: haste means speed, so in haste is quickly

indicators.note: beginning means just the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A signal to go both ways and start pointing quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Signal is a brand of toothpaste, hence the question mark. 'to', joining the P of 'beginning' onto the word for quickly, is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal is a well-known brand name of toothpaste, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Get through a state capital via whichever route

parts.note: to get by is to get through, so by means through
NY abbreviates New York State
capital is money, and means are financial resources

explanation.surface: Travel to a state capital however you can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state capital' suggests a city such as Albany, but 'state' is NY and 'capital' is money.
explanation.definitionFit: By any means is an idiom for in whatever way possible.

clue.text: Pulmonary vein's blood is taken round next day, for example, in circulation

parts.note: a round thing is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: circulation suggests going round and mixing, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical note says blood from the lungs is carried around the body the following day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in circulation' scrambles NEXTDAYEG into XYGENATED. 'is taken' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: The pulmonary vein carries blood that has just picked up oxygen in the lungs.

clue.text: South of Angolan capital, first of volunteers and relative get lost!

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means coming below, after the other piece
capital means the first, upper-case letter of the word
first of means just the opening letter

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: In southern Angola, volunteers and relatives are told to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an archaic command meaning go away.

clue.text: Bird checked the call of another

indicators.note: checked means stopped short, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a coot is a waterbird

explanation.surface: Someone checks on a bird while listening to another bird's call.
explanation.walkthrough: The other bird is the dove or pigeon, whose call this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A coo is the soft call made by doves and pigeons, a different bird from the coot.

clue.text: Schedule has to advance ambition primarily, being driven?

indicators.note: has means holds within, so one piece contains the rest

parts.note: a car is something that is driven
to advance money is to lend it

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter only

explanation.surface: A timetable driven by ambition to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being driven?' is a definition by example of a car, hence the question mark. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a schedule of dates and events.

clue.text: Barrel the addict knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or addict, as in fitness nut

explanation.surface: A drinker who knocked back a whole barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for wine or beer.

clue.text: What may tether sheep proves shaky

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a shackle is a fetter that can tether an animal

explanation.surface: A farmer finds the restraint for the flock is wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ramshackle is rickety and falling apart.

clue.text: Dog perhaps bites man, one picking nits?

indicators.note: bites means holds in the jaws, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dog is one example of a pet
Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A tabloid twist: dog bites man, then grooms for nits.
explanation.walkthrough: Nit-picking is fussing over tiny errors, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over minor details, which is nit-picking.

clue.text: Bail out sovereign with money — bread

parts.note: to bail out water is to pump it out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher
a nickel is a US five-cent coin, money

explanation.surface: A bailout for the monarch with cash goes on a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bail out' suggests a financial rescue, but it means pumping water out. 'with' is part of the money leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dark, dense German rye bread.

clue.text: It employs men on board red ship

parts.note: Che Guevara was a famous red, a communist
SS is the prefix steamship

explanation.surface: A communist on a ship employs the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The men are chess pieces on a board, not sailors on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is played with pieces called men moved on a board.

clue.text: Song delivered invention

definitions.meaning: a German art song of the Romantic period

explanation.definitionFit: A lied is a German art song, and lied is the past tense of telling untruths.

clue.text: Complete bounder from Oxford?

definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a laced shoe, which has a back part raised under the foot

explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a cad, and the raised back of a shoe such as an Oxford.

clue.text: Male drinking beer cut short in place of confinement

indicators.note: drinking means taking something inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a stag is an adult male deer, and a stag party is all-male

indicators.note: cut short means losing the final letter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A man downing an incomplete pint while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the final E off the beer before 'drinking' puts it inside. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.

clue.text: Phone call impossible, given cutoff point

definitions.meaning: a dead telephone line makes calling impossible
a time limit after which nothing more is accepted

explanation.definitionFit: Deadline means a time limit, and read as two words it is a phone line with no tone.

clue.text: Fake it in the name of frequency, though less hot

indicators.note: in places the word for it inside the other piece
less means without, so the letter for hot is dropped

parts.note: the hertz is the unit of frequency, named after Heinrich Hertz
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Someone forges something in a physicist's name, but cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the old slang for sex appeal, a crossword staple. 'though' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means substitute or imitation, an inferior stand-in for the real thing.

clue.text: Short length needed, by the way, for pastry

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
being short with someone is being rude

explanation.surface: A baker says a short length is needed for the pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short length' looks like one measurement, but 'Short' is RUDE and 'length' L. 'needed, by' are link words placing ST beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a layered pastry, often with apple filling.
